key_insight: PixelSmile introduces a diffusion-based framework that disentangles fine-grained facial expression semantics via fully symmetric joint training, enabled by a new continuously annotated dataset and benchmark to measure subtle editing performance.
problem_solved: Overcomes intrinsic semantic overlap that prevents precise, controllable, and identity-preserving fine-grained facial expression editing.
method: Construct FFE (Flex Facial Expression) dataset with continuous affective annotations to capture subtle expression variations.
Establish FFE-Bench to quantify structural confusion, editing accuracy, linear controllability, and the trade-off between expression editing and identity preservation.
Propose PixelSmile: a diffusion framework using fully symmetric joint training to disentangle expression semantics and enable fine-grained, controllable edits while maintaining identity.
impact: Provides practitioners with a dataset, benchmark, and a model that enable more precise and controllable facial expression edits, improving realism and identity preservation for applications in graphics, AR/VR, and human-centric AI.
visual_elements: Continuous affect annotation strip (color gradient) showing how FFE maps expressions along continuous axes
Pipeline diagram of PixelSmile: input face → diffusion-based encoder/decoder with symmetric joint-training module → edited output (with disentangled expression latent)
Benchmark charts: radar or bar charts comparing structural confusion, editing accuracy, linear controllability, and identity preservation across methods
Before/after example grid highlighting subtle expression edits and identity consistency
paper_title: PixelSmile: Toward Fine-Grained Facial Expression Editing
paper_authors: Jiabin Hua, Hengyuan Xu, Aojie Li, Wei Cheng, Gang Yu
